collection.credit: NEW EVENTS — INNER LIFE, PART VIII (141-160, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)

ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: A villager's old digging stick, worn to the shape of their hands, snaps clean in two: mend it, or make a new one.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s digging stick has been with (subject.him/her) for years. The handle is worn smooth in exactly the shape of (subject.his/her) hands. Today, halfway through a hard bit of ground, it snaps clean in two. (subject) stands holding the two halves, feeling unexpectedly sad about a stick.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (subject) binds the halves together with cord, very carefully. It holds, sort of. It wobbles a bit now, and the handle has a lump in it. (subject.He/She) keeps using it anyway. (friend) offers (subject.him/her) a new one. "No thank you," says (subject). "We're used to each other."

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) finds a good straight branch and spends the evening shaping a new digging stick. It's fine. It works. It doesn't feel like anything. But by the end of the season (subject) notices that the handle has started to wear smooth, just a little, in exactly the shape of (subject.his/her) hands.
